description: Hearth's PROTECTED BOUNDARIES and SENSORY LAW, tested
note: These laws are about what this app will never do to a family. Refusals are testable as absences; a guard's value is the day it fires.
trap_handled: The text most likely to contain a banned word is the text banning it. Comments stripped, negations refused, the definition site never scanned for its own list, and UI COPY read rather than identifiers.

guards.law: OVERWHELM_PAUSE_MS — never configurable, never shortened, no setting
guards.note: A reassignment outside the definition site is what 'configurable' would look like arriving.

guards.law: code identifiers and overwhelm_events keep legacy names ON PURPOSE — do not 'clean up' to match the family-facing name Sattva
guards.note: A KEEP-rule, not a ban. A guard that wanted these gone would enforce the opposite of the law.

guards.law: the signals table holds CURRENT state only — never a signal-history table; presence is now, not a log
the app NEVER makes sound, NEVER vibrates, has NO push notifications
banned in UI copy: overdue, streak, productivity, late, failed (CLAUDE.md: grep before shipping)
guards.note: UI COPY only — markup and quoted strings, comments stripped, negations refused, and the file that DEFINES the list never scanned for it. The text most likely to contain a forbidden word is the text forbidding it.

guards.law: prefers-reduced-motion turns breathing pulses into steady glows
no network calls anywhere in v1 (license §7 — structural, not aspirational)
four explicit sql:allow-* capabilities · no non-ASCII SQL DEFAULTs
